---
title: "Quiz: Check and repair data"
---

[Exercises](11-data-quality.qmd) · [Lecture slides](../lectures/11-data-quality/lec.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** The file is intended to have one row per plant. It has 25 rows but 24 unique
plant IDs. What should you inspect before removing a row?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Compare every field in the repeated records and consult the source notes.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Inspect the repeated ID's full records and the source notes. Here both P01
records are identical and the recorder confirms an import duplicate. In a
time-series table, a repeated plant ID could be legitimate.
:::

---

**Q2.** P21 has a final length of 4.38. Which evidence justifies changing it to 43.8 mm?

(i) Other plants are larger.  

(ii) The correction increases the group mean.  

(iii) The original source record gives 43.8 mm.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A surprising value suggests a check; it does not specify the correct value.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(iii). The source record supports this correction. Size or a preferred result
alone does not establish an error.
:::

---

**Q3.** P06 started at 24.7 mm and its final measurement is missing. What growth
would replacing the missing final value with zero produce? What should the
cleaned table retain?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Growth is final minus initial. A missing value states that the measurement
is unavailable.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
It would invent $0 - 24.7 = -24.7$ mm growth. Retain `NA` for final length
and growth; there is no supported replacement.
:::

---

**Q4.** After repair there are 12 plant records in each group, with one control
growth unavailable. What are the available growth sample sizes?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Count observed values separately from enrolled plant records.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
11 controls and 12 treated plants have observed growth. Both groups still
contain 12 plant records. `sum(!is.na(growth_mm))` counts available growths.
:::

---

**Q5.** Which files allow you to reproduce and explain a repair?

(i) Only the cleaned CSV.  

(ii) Raw CSV, source notes, and repair script.  

(iii) A screenshot of RStudio.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A reproducible repair needs both its input and the reasons for changing it.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(ii). The script regenerates derived data from the original, and the source
notes explain the correction evidence.
:::
